name: Hospitality, Restaurant and Event Manager
description: ⚠⚠⚠ Lodging managers earn $69,250 and food service managers $69,390 — $140 apart — but 72% of employers want a bachelor's for the first and 30% will take a high school diploma for the second. ⚠⚠ And food service management is SEVEN TIMES the occupation: 352,800 jobs against 52,000, with 42,000 annual openings against 5,400. In the industry Florida is built on, the degree buys you the smaller half at the same money.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ NOTHING IN THIS FAMILY IS LICENSED, AND THE DEGREE IS NOT THE GATE. O*NET's employer data: lodging managers 72% bachelor's; food service managers 30% high school diploma, 21% postsecondary certificate, 19% associate degree; meeting and event planners 41% bachelor's. ⚠ Only the lodging side treats the degree as standard, and lodging is the smallest of the three occupations. ⚠⚠⚠ WHAT THE BACHELOR'S ACTUALLY BUYS is the corporate and lodging track — brand management roles, revenue management, multi-property and head-office posts — and speed of promotion. It does not buy entry, because entry in this industry is a job, and everyone starts on a shift. ⚠ The operational credentials that DO get named in postings are short and cheap: food-safety manager certification (ServSafe or an equivalent recognised in Florida), responsible-vendor alcohol training, and for events the CMP, which requires documented experience rather than a degree. ⚠⚠ Florida requires a certified food protection manager on staff at licensed food service establishments, so that certification is a practical requirement of the job rather than an optional extra — get it early, it is inexpensive, and it appears in entry-level postings.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ The same money, and one of them asks for a degree

RoleSOC2025 medianEmployedOpenings/yrGrowth 2024–34Entry
Lodging manager11-9081$69,250⚠ 52,000⚠ 5,400average (3–4%)⚠⚠ 72% bachelor's
✅ Food service manager11-9051✅ $69,390✅ 352,800✅ 42,000✅ faster (5–6%)✅ 30% high school, 21% certificate, 19% associate
Meeting and event planner13-1121$61,160155,80015,500faster (5–6%)41% bachelor's

⚠⚠⚠ Read the top two rows together, because they are the whole decision. The medians differ by $140. But food service management is seven times the occupation, has nearly eight times the annual openings, is growing faster, and mostly does not ask for a degree.

⚠⚠ That does not make the degree worthless — it makes it a purchase with a specific purpose. It buys the corporate and lodging track: brand roles, revenue management, multi-property and head-office posts, and faster promotion. It does not buy entry, because entry here is a job and everybody starts on a shift.

⚠⚠ Florida's hospitality education is in two cities

InstitutionCredentials (2023)
Florida International University667
University of Central Florida590
Florida State University224
Valencia College64
Florida Atlantic University51

⚠⚠⚠ FIU and UCF together are 72% of the state's output — which is Miami and Orlando, which is the cruise industry and the theme parks. The education sits exactly where the industry does, and that is an advantage if you are there and a relocation decision if you are not.

⚠ The short credentials are spread far more widely. Hotel/Motel Administration is 251 credentials at 12 institutions, all certificates, led by Valencia at 97 and Broward at 53; restaurant and food service management adds 105 at 13; the catering and combined-operations codes another 49 at 9. Those are state and technical colleges, and they are the cheap way in.

⚠⚠⚠ Event planning is one university

Meeting and Event Planning is 157 credentials at TWO Florida public institutions — 140 of them UCF bachelor's and 17 FAU certificates.

⚠ It is the narrowest door in the family and effectively a single programme. But the occupation is 155,800 jobs with 15,500 annual openings and only 41% of employers reporting a bachelor's — so most event planners did not come through it.

⚠⚠ The credential the industry actually names is the CMP, and it requires documented experience rather than a degree. The realistic route is to work events — hotels, convention centres, venues, associations — and credential afterwards. HFT2750 The Event Industry is carried by 13 Florida institutions if you want the coursework cheaply.

⚠⚠ The certification that is a practical requirement

Florida requires a certified food protection manager on staff at licensed food service establishments. That is not an optional extra; it appears in entry-level postings, it is inexpensive, and it is a day.

⚠ Get it before you need it. Along with responsible-vendor alcohol training, it is the cheapest thing on this page that changes whether you are hireable, and it costs a fraction of a single course.

⚠ A warning about the course numbers in this subject

This site's own catalogue work has found the HFT prefix to be among the most confused in Florida. Three documented cases:

  • HFT4274 — the statewide title says Resort Management; FGCU teaches Vacation Ownership and Timeshare and FIU Short-Term Rental / Vacation Ownership. Two institutions agreeing with each other against the state label.
  • HFT4252 — the statewide title says employee wellbeing and the statewide description is entirely hotel and resort management. UCF teaches the title, Pensacola State teaches the description.
  • ⚠⚠⚠ HFT3271 — statewide Condo/Resort Management, and the three carriers teach nightclub management (FIU), club management (FGCU) and spa management (UWF). Four readings, and no carrier teaches the statewide one.

⚠⚠ The practical instruction: in this prefix, register by reading the syllabus rather than the title, and on transfer send the syllabus rather than the course number. An evaluator matching HFT3271 to HFT3271 is matching two different subjects.

Necessary skills

  • Cost control. Food cost, labour cost, occupancy — the managers who hold these move up and the ones who do not, do not. FSS2500 Food Service Costing and Controls exists for this.
  • Scheduling a workforce that turns over constantly, in an industry where that is the normal condition rather than a crisis.
  • Revenue management — pricing rooms and covers against demand. The highest-leverage skill in the industry and the most transferable.
  • Service recovery. O*NET puts resolving guest complaints first among a lodging manager's tasks, and it is a taught skill rather than a temperament.
  • Regulatory literacy: food safety, alcohol, accessibility, employment law.
  • Stamina for the hours. Evenings, weekends and holidays are when this industry works, and the pay does not carry a premium for them.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Do not buy the bachelor's to become a restaurant manager. Same median as lodging, seven times the jobs, and 70% of employers do not ask for one. Buy it if you want the corporate and lodging track, and know that is what you are buying.

⚠⚠ Get the food protection manager certification now. It is required on staff at licensed establishments in Florida, it takes a day, and it appears in entry-level postings.

⚠ If you are outside Miami or Orlando, price the relocation honestly. FIU and UCF are 72% of the degree output. A state-college certificate near home plus a job may beat a distant bachelor's plus debt, especially given what the food service numbers say.

⚠⚠ Learn revenue management deliberately, whatever your title. It is the one skill in this industry that scales with the size of the property and travels between hotels, restaurants, cruise and attractions.

And take the internship courses seriously rather than as a formality. HFT2942 Hospitality Internship II is carried by 10 Florida institutions, and in an industry that hires on demonstrated shifts rather than transcripts, the placement is the credential.

programs.note: The family — 23 Florida public institutions across six codes. ⚠⚠ The general bachelor's is concentrated: FIU 667 and UCF 590 are 72% of the state's output. ⚠ The short certificates (Hotel/Motel Administration, 251 credentials at 12 institutions, all certificates) are spread far more widely and are the cheap way in.

⚠⚠ The more portable substitute, and one a great many hospitality managers actually hold. A business degree with operations and finance coursework competes for the same corporate posts and is taught at far more Florida institutions. ⚠ Hospitality wins on industry knowledge and internship networks; business wins if you might leave the industry.

⚠ Revenue management — pricing rooms and covers against demand — is the highest-leverage skill in this industry and it is a marketing discipline. HFT2500 Hospitality and Tourism Marketing is carried by 10 Florida institutions.
⚠ Named because this is a margin business: food cost, labour cost and occupancy are what a manager is measured on, and FSS2500 Food Service Costing and Controls is where Florida teaches it.

⚠ Not a route — named as an honest comparison for a student weighing service-sector management degrees. $123,860 against lodging's $69,250, 24 Florida institutions with 20 state colleges carrying the upper-division work, and no two-city concentration.

courses.reason: ⚠ Introduction to Hospitality and Tourism — 21 Florida public institutions, by far the most widely carried course in the field and available at state colleges across the state. The cheap way to test the subject.

The Event Industry — 13 institutions. ⚠ Named because event planning as a DEGREE exists at only two Florida institutions, so this course is how most people get the coursework without relocating to Orlando.
⚠⚠ Hospitality and Tourism Marketing — 10 institutions. Revenue management lives here, and it is the highest-leverage and most transferable skill in the industry.
Hospitality Law — 10 institutions. Liability, alcohol, accessibility and employment law, all of which a manager carries personally.
Front Office Management — 9 institutions. The operational core of lodging, and the department most managers come up through.
Human Resource Management for Hospitality — 7 institutions. Scheduling and turnover are the daily reality of the job, and this is where they are taught as a discipline rather than a problem.
⚠⚠ Hospitality Internship II — 10 institutions. In an industry that hires on demonstrated shifts rather than transcripts, the placement is the credential.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered HFT2949 Internship Exploration and Work Experience at 7 institutions. Register by number.

courses.reason: ⚠ Food Service Costing and Controls — 6 institutions. Food cost and labour cost are what a food service manager is measured on, and this is the single most directly employable course on the page.
Garde Manger — 7 institutions, the most widely carried culinary course in the state. Named for students heading to the kitchen side rather than the office.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ The culinary programmes themselves are coded under culinary arts, which this site cannot yet represent — see the chef path when it lands.

courses.reason: Food Preparation for Catered Events — 6 institutions including UCF. The practical bridge between the culinary and event sides.
Financial Accounting — 32 institutions. Hospitality is a margin business and a manager who cannot read a P&L does not get a second property.
Principles of Marketing — 24 institutions, all state colleges. Useful here for the demand and pricing content.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ A 2000-level course cannot supply upper-division hours toward a Florida baccalaureate. If a hospitality bachelor's is the plan, check whether your programme wants MAR3023 instead — see the Marketing Manager path.

courses.reason: Fundamentals of Speech Communication — 16 institutions. Service recovery, staff briefing and client presentation are the job in three different registers.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Required for any degree route, and incident reports and contracts are written documents with consequences.

⚠ Elementary Spanish I — named for Florida specifically. In Miami, Orlando and most Florida kitchens and housekeeping departments, Spanish is an operational skill rather than a cultural one, and managers who have it supervise better.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers beginning Spanish several ways (SPN1120, SPN1130C, SPN1000). Any of them serves the purpose.

Tasks include resolving guest complaints about policies and services, setting room rates and departmental budgets, coordinating between managers, and supervising staff performance.

sources.label: O*NET — Food Service Managers (11-9051.00)
sources.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The comparison this page turns on: 352,800 employed — SEVEN TIMES lodging management — median $69,390, within $140 of it, with 42,000 annual openings against 5,400, and growth faster than average (5% to 6%). ⚠ Education 30% high school diploma, 21% postsecondary certificate, 19% associate degree. The bigger, faster-growing half of the industry does not ask for the degree.

sources.label: O*NET — Meeting, Convention, and Event Planners (13-1121.00)
sources.note: 155,800 employed, median $61,160 (2025), 15,500 annual openings, growth faster than average (5% to 6%), and only 41% of employers reporting a bachelor's. ⚠ Set that against Florida's supply: event planning as a degree exists at TWO public institutions, 140 of the 157 credentials being UCF bachelor's — so most event planners did not come through a specialist programme.

Hotel/Motel Administration (52.0904): 251 at 12 institutions, ALL certificates. Restaurant/Food Services (52.0905): 105 at 13. Meeting and Event Planning (52.0907): 157 at just 2, 140 of them UCF bachelor's. Resort Management (52.0906): 68, FGCU alone.
